payload.choice_traced:
THE WINNER IS X3 - git as the only search provider, ZERO new dependencies - and it traces to the weighted criteria through TWO recorded Pugh runs, the second existing because a probe invalidated the first.

DATUM CHOICE: the strongest viable RIVAL, X1 (ripgrep + git), not the status quo. The status quo was disqualified before scoring on the C2 REACH veto - today's surface cannot reach refs or outside sources, so killer story S1 is impossible on it rather than slow. A status-quo datum run was therefore neither needed nor legitimate: there is no worth-doing-at-all question when the incumbent fails a veto.

RUN 1 (datum X1): X3 net -3, X2 net -11. X1 led. Recorded with a discrepancy worth keeping: a SIGN-ONLY Pugh table would have put X3 ahead (two pluses on weight-5 criteria against minuses on weight-4 and weight-3), and only the magnitudes put X1 in front. A three-point lead inside my own scoring noise, with X1's decisive advantage scored from DOCUMENTATION because rg is not installed here - not a defensible convergence.

THE PROBE (run-477ac3e1031a): rather than converge on the assumption, I tested it. `git grep -z` returns three NUL-separated fields with no separator ambiguity - which was the entirety of ripgrep's structured-output advantage.

RUN 2 (datum X1, C4 rescored on evidence): X3 net +5. Absolute totals X3 106, X1 101, X2 90.

TRACING TO CRITERIA: X3 wins C3 one-click install (nothing to install) and C5 one-implementation-per-job (ONE tool for tree and record, where X1 needs two tools with two output shapes to answer one question). It loses C4 and C6, both accepted knowingly and both surfacing again as at-risk quality scenarios. C7 and C8 are equal, so the guidance decision rides separately on se.adr-applies-to-becomes-a-selector.

AND THE REVERSAL IS ON THE RECORD: this contradicts the owner's stated expectation that we would take ripgrep. It is within their instruction - 'do prior art research when you make your decision, and if you find a better solution use that' - and the better solution turned out to be no dependency at all. Flagged here and surfaced again at gate_release rather than left to be discovered in a diff.
payload.sensitivity_ruled:
VERDICT: WEIGHT-SENSITIVE. Not robust, and I am not calling it robust. Five points separate the winner from the runner-up out of ~106, and I hunted for the losing world rather than for reassurance.

THREE FLIPS FOUND. FLIP 1: raise C4 to 5, or score X3's C4 at 3 - X1 wins. Credibility MODERATE-TO-HIGH, because X3's C4=4 rests on one probe against one repo with ASCII-ish content that my own probe then mangled by reading latin1. FLIP 2: the untracked-files default proves costly or awkward - then C1 FRESHNESS becomes conditional, and C1 is a veto, so X3 is eliminated rather than out-scored. Credibility LOW-TO-MODERATE. FLIP 3: C5 drops from 5 to 3 if the owner meant the no-duplicate-code ruling narrowly (no dead fallback) rather than broadly (never two tools for one job) - X1 wins. Credibility MODERATE, and it is an interpretation of intent, which is precisely what I got wrong three times yesterday.

WHAT DOES NOT FLIP: no reweighting rescues X2 (its deficit is weight-5 against a weight-2 gain) and none rescues the datum (a veto is not a weight).

TRIPWIRES IN RAID: se.raid-git-grep-tracked-files-only (FLIP 2 made concrete, with the default INVERTED at our boundary as its standing mitigation and a named test); se.raid-a-requirement-may-yet-demand-ripgrep (the accepted ceiling - multiline, submatch spans, ignored files - with the explicit instruction NOT to bend git grep around a multiline need with heuristics, since that recreates the searcher this iteration deletes).

ROUTED TO M5 RATHER THAN THE REGISTER, because a spike this milestone will answer them: the NUL-parsing robustness that FLIP 1 turns on, and whether semantic matching picks the rules that bind a state (X2's survival rests on it).
ROUTED TO THE OWNER: FLIP 3, my reading of their ruling, which carries the winner's largest margin.
payload.matrix_review:
KILLER - the baseline reviewed as DATA.

DECOMPOSITION: eight elements over 28 functions. E1 search facade, E2 range reader, E3 honest-answer layer, E4 file writer, E5 packet builder, E6 lint registry, E7 record keeper, E8 settings lane. Each has a black-box contract stating what it takes, what it gives, and what it may NEVER do - the never-clause being the part that makes a contract checkable rather than descriptive.

CLUSTERING: six function clusters, cut by coupling density under ONE declared relation meaning (Fi->Fj means Fj needs something Fi produces or establishes) with every edge classified data / contract / sequence / resource. Two cuts are justified by failure mode rather than tidiness. (1) K2 HONESTY is separate from K1 RETRIEVAL and sits ABOVE it: if honesty lives inside retrieval, each provider grows its own idea of what a non-answer looks like - which is exactly how a missing argument once produced a confident search for the word 'undefined'. (2) K6 was TORN at consolidation into E7 record and E8 settings; I flagged that cluster as loose at partitioning and the tear was taken, because the two share no data, no lifecycle and no failure mode - E8 is machine-local and uncommitted, E7 is the committed record.

ALLOCATION: 28 functions, 28 allocations, each exactly once - counted, not eyeballed. The one that could have gone elsewhere is F9 REPORT INCOMPLETENESS: E2 knows an oversize read's true size, so F9 could sit there, but it sits with the other honesty functions because incompleteness is a property of an ANSWER rather than of a reader - search results are capped too, and two providers reporting incompleteness would grow two dialects of 'there is more'. F28 record-what-was-consulted sits in E7 for the mirror reason: logging is a property of the record, not of the reader.

INTERFACES: seven, each declared at both ends except two that CANNOT be, and those are named rather than hidden. I3 and I4 cross to git, which cannot declare anything back - ASYMMETRIC BY NATURE, and the place a git version change would bite; the only defence is that we own the arguments and the parsing. I5 (E5 <-> E6) is THE LOAD-BEARING interface: a rule supplied to the agent and a rule enforced by a lint must be the same rule, held by a shared selector vocabulary at both ends. The partitioning named that edge as the constraint any candidate had to satisfy, and it survived into the baseline.

NO ELEMENT REACHES INSIDE ANOTHER: E6's lints read through E1/E2 like any other caller, so caps, containment and logging apply to lints too and a lint cannot quietly become a second reader with its own rules.

ONE HONEST WEAKNESS: two interfaces cross to the same external tool, so a git output change moves both at once. Visible in the scoring as C4's residual risk, mitigated by an M5 spike rather than by a design change.

NO NEW ELEMENT WAS NEEDED during evaluation. If one is found during the build it returns HERE, and I expect the likeliest candidate to be a migration helper for the applies_to rewrite - which is why I am naming it now rather than discovering it as a surprise.
payload.evaluation_recorded:
EIGHT QUALITY SCENARIOS WALKED: five addressed, two at-risk, one unaddressed-by-construction. All three verdicts used.

ADDRESSED: QS1 freshness (carried by se.adr-untracked-files-are-searched-by-default - and it was AT-RISK until that ADR, since git's own default would have failed the agent's most common pattern silently); QS2 guidance arrives (conditional on the ten-node migration, with the honest note that authoring discipline can let it rot later); QS4 no lint parks a run (addressed STRUCTURALLY - the verdict type has three members and none blocks, which beats a rule asking authors to be careful); QS5 audit distinguishes computed from asserted; QS7 the record survives carelessness (the strongest, because it rests on the merge's second parent - a property, not a procedure).

AT RISK, and scored so deliberately: QS3 the packet stays readable - E5 REPORTS guidance volume but does not BOUND it, and 'we will see it happen' is weaker than 'it cannot happen'. QS6 no search floods or hangs - git grep provides no native caps, so every bound is ours to build and can be forgotten in one path; weaker than ripgrep would have been, accepted knowingly at C6.

UNADDRESSED BY CONSTRUCTION: QS8 the lane beats the alternative. No architecture can carry it; it is measured on the NEXT iteration as workarounds-per-iteration. Named rather than quietly dropped.

ONE RESIDUE INSIDE AN ADDRESSED SCENARIO: QS5 proves a check RAN and what it found, never that it was WORTH running. A weak lint reporting pass looks identical to a strong one from the auditor's seat. Not fixable at this interface; it belongs to review.

Seven fitness candidates named for M7, and the three that CANNOT automate are named too.
payload.adrs_traced:
SIX DECIDING ADRs, each naming the requirements and criteria that forced it, each recording what was rejected and why.

se.adr-git-is-the-only-searcher -> R3, R4, R5, R6, C1, C2, C3, C5. se.adr-locate-and-read-are-separate -> R1, R3, C4. se.adr-untracked-files-are-searched-by-default -> C1 (veto), R3. se.adr-applies-to-becomes-a-selector -> R14, R15, C7, C8. se.adr-a-lint-decides-or-defers -> R16, R17, R18, R19 and se.law-responsibility-never-delegates. se.adr-the-hash-is-the-pointer-the-tag-is-the-name -> R22, R23, R24, R25 and R5.

Tracing lives in the ADR text rather than in edges because the requirements are evidence prose rather than ledger nodes - the engine refused set_field on `addresses` and `rejected` as edge kinds, which is a small live proof that the guard rails work.

THREE OF THE SIX ARE FORCED BY SOMETHING OBSERVED rather than argued, which is the difference between this set and a set of preferences: the searcher ADR by run-477ac3e1031a, the untracked-files ADR by git's documented default meeting the agent's measured behaviour, and the hash/tag ADR by two observations - lightweight tags being dropped by push.followTags, and git's own 'refname is ambiguous' warning during a probe.

NO ADR was written for the batch-patch shape, se_config, or required-arg enforcement: one obvious realization each, no contested alternative, and an ADR for a decision nobody could have made differently is decision theatre. Recorded as a judgement so it does not read as a gap.
